reviewers.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY: the printed cell is $64,466 (in $000s), Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Parks & Roads Services, Program Summary, Snow and Ice Control, row 'Expenditure & Transfers', column '2022 Budget', printed page 212 (PDF page 216). Ratio 100,000/64,466 = 1.551 -> Partially supported under the primary cutoffs (1.5 to <1.8; the failing part is the word 'double', the figure is about 1.55 times, or 'half again'). Under the alternative cutoffs (Supported >=1.7; Partially 1.25 to <1.7) also Partially supported. Same page: row 'Revenue & Transfers' $13, 'Intra-municipal Recoveries' ($800), 'Total Net Operating Requirement' $63,653 (2022). ALTERNATIVE A (cell plus every council amendment to the 2022 Snow and Ice Control budget in force on 2022-12-12): I found three council-approved 2022 additions, all one-time: (1) 2022-03-14, City Council, carry-forward of $2.3 million of 2021 Snow and Ice Control surplus into 2022 (recorded in the Spring 2022 SOBA report FCS01143 as 'approved by Council on March 14, 2022'); (2) 2022-04-19, City Council, Spring 2022 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment FCS01143 Attachment 1, 'Enhanced Snow Clearing Pilot costs (total costs of $16.6 M, less $2.3M from 2021 program surplus...)', +$14,300 thousand expense funded from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, motion carried 13-0; (3) 2022-07-04, City Council item CO01277, 'That the Parks and Roads Services Branch budget be increased by $4.7 million, from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, on a one time basis to fund the Snow and Ice Control program for the 2022 portion of the upcoming winter season', carried 13-0. The Fall 2021 SOBA (FCS, November 2021) contains no Snow and Ice Control change to the 2022 budget. Alternative A = 64,466 + 2,300 + 14,300 + 4,700 = $85,766 thousand; ratio 1.166 -> Contradicted under the primary cutoffs (<1.5) and Contradicted under the alternative cutoffs (<1.25). Cross-check: the City's own year-end 'Snow and Ice Control' 2022 adjusted expense budget in the Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022 (FCS01656 Attachment 1, page 38 of the PDF, in $000s) is $79,474 (revenue budget $23,108, net budget ($56,366)); on that figure the ratio is 1.258 -> Contradicted under the primary cutoffs, Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs (1.25 to <1.7). If only the 2022-07-04 amendment is counted (the reading the brief named), 64,466 + 4,700 = 69,166, ratio 1.446 -> Contradicted (primary cutoffs), Partially supported (alternative cutoffs). ALTERNATIVE B (2023 Budget): the cell the brief names does not exist: the City's 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans contains no Snow and Ice Control program summary table; the Parks and Roads Services branch section lists Snow and Ice Control only as a service description and the enhanced-standards service package. Council's December 2022 Operating Budget Amendment 18 (carried 12-1, M. Janz opposed) funded the 'Enhanced Snow and Ice Control Service Standards' package at 20 per cent: 2023 $274,600 (Community Standards and Neighbourhoods) and $3,768,000 (Parks and Roads Services); 2024 $3,724,800; 2025 $2,476,800; 2026 $721,400; the printed service package table (2023-2026 Operating Budget, page 105) shows $4,043 (2023), $3,725 (2024), $2,477 (2025), $721 (2026) in $000s. The closest City-published 2023 snow budget figure is the Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2023 (FCS02229 Attachment 1, supplemental page 1 of 7): Snow and Ice Control 2023 expense budget $63,574 thousand (actual $54,917; net budget ($61,173), net actual ($52,555)); this is the budget as adjusted at year-end, not the December 2022 approved figure. Media reported the December 2022 approved 2023 total as $60.9 million (Global News 2022-12-20; CBC 2022-12-16: base $56.9 million plus $4 million). Ratios: 100,000/63,574 = 1.573 and 100,000/60,900 = 1.642 -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets. NET AND ACTUAL CONTEXT (not denominators): printed 2022 Total Net Operating Requirement $63,653 thousand -> 1.571; City year-end 2022 adjusted net budget ($56,366) -> 1.774; 2022 actual Snow and Ice Control expense $97,571 thousand (net actual ($74,607)), Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022 -> 1.025 on actual. DEFINITION SENSITIVITY: the verdict is Partially supported on the primary cell but Contradicted on the budget as amended in-year (Alternative A); the finding is definition-sensitive and neither side can cite it without that qualification. The three one-time 2022 additions were extraordinary responses to a bad winter and a residential blading pilot; the ongoing base budget (printed cell, or the 2023 approved figure) gives 1.55 to 1.64 either way. QUOTATION CONTEXT: the advocacy page (live 2026-09-02; Wayback Machine availability API confirms a capture at 2022-12-12 05:58:23 UTC) reads 'In fact, it's almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget!' and 'the $100 million he wants to spend on Bike Lanes is almost 5 times the amount he wants to spend on affordable housing'; the page names no snow figure. Context only: the December 2022 affordable housing land amendment reported by CBC was $22.9 million (100/22.9 = 4.4x) and Table 8's 'Affordable Housing and Homelessness Service' 2023-2026 capital line is $49.2 million (2.0x).

The primary denominator is the 2022 approved base budget ($64.47M). Alternative A includes the July 2022 amendment (+$4.7M), bringing the total to $69.17M. Alternative B is the 2023 base budget ($60.9M). The ratio under the primary denominator is 1.55, falling into the 'Partially supported' range (1.5 to 1.8). Under Alternative A, the ratio drops to 1.45 (Contradicted). Under Alternative B, it is 1.64 (Partially supported). The word 'double' is an overstatement under all readings.

The approved operating budget prints the 2022 Snow and Ice Control Expenditure & Transfers cell as $64.466 million ($64,466 in thousands). The resulting ratio is $100 million / $64.466 million = 1.551. Under the brief's primary cutoffs, this is Partially supported: the amount is substantially larger, but the specific phrase "almost double" fails because 1.551 is below 1.8. It is also Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs. Alternative A adds council's July 4, 2022 one-time $4.7 million increase, producing an amended gross budget of $69.166 million and a ratio of 1.446; that is Contradicted under the primary cutoffs and Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs. The published $60.9 million 2023 snow-clearing figure produces a ratio of 1.642, Partially supported under both cutoff sets; the consulted record did not establish with sufficient precision whether that fact-sheet figure incorporates every December 2022 amendment to the named program cell. The comparison mixes a four-year capital authorization with one year of operating expenditure. On a like-for-like 2023 basis, CM-20-0330's approved $5.950 million allocation was 9.77% of the published $60.9 million snow budget, not approximately double. The profile's approved allocations, printed in thousands, were $5.950 million in 2023, $26.750 million in 2024, $33.650 million in 2025 and $33.650 million in 2026, averaging $25 million per approved year. The $100 million divided by the 2022 net operating requirement of $63.653 million is 1.571. Reported CM-20-0330 actuals were $0.807 million in 2023 and $9.689 million in 2024, calculated as $10.496 million cumulative at 2024 year-end less $0.807 million cumulative at 2023 year-end. Cumulative actual expenditure was $25.093 million at September 30, 2025, implying $14.597 million during January-September 2025. Against gross Snow and Ice Control actual expenditure, the completed-year ratios were $0.807 million / $51.750 million = 1.56% for 2023 and $9.689 million / $64.749 million = 14.96% for 2024. The completed-year CM-20-0330 actual average for 2023-2024 was $5.248 million per year. A spring 2025 adjustment transferred $0.430 million from CM-20-0330, reducing its current budget to $99.570 million; it does not change what council approved in December 2022.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes: Verdict figure. Numerator: CM-20-0330 approved at $100,000 thousand (Appendix A printed page 103, in $000s; profile sheet pages 540-543; Council Capital Budget Amendment 7, carried 9 to 4, minutes of City Council - Budget November 30 to December 16, 2022, where the profile is named 'Bike Plan Implementation - Approach 3'). Per-year approved: 5,950 (2023), 26,750 (2024), 33,650 (2025), 33,650 (2026); approved average $25.0 million a year. One later amendment: Spring 2025 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment (FCS02852, City Council June 10, 2025) moved $430 thousand to profile 25-25-9506 Dunluce Neighbourhood and Alley Renewal, leaving 99,570. Primary denominator: Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Parks & Roads Services, Program Summary, Snow and Ice Control, row 'Expenditure & Transfers', column '2022 Budget', printed page 212 (PDF 216), 64,466 in $000s. Ratio 100,000 / 64,466 = 1.551. Primary cutoffs: Partially supported (1.5 to below 1.8). Alternative cutoffs: Partially supported (1.25 to below 1.7). Alternative A, budget as amended in-year: I found three council additions to the 2022 Snow and Ice Control budget in force on 2022-12-12, each one-time: (1) March 14, 2022, $2.3 million of 2021 program surplus applied to 2022 costs; (2) April 19, 2022, Spring 2022 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment, FCS01143 Attachment 1, 'Enhanced Snow Clearing Pilot costs', expense 14,300 funded from the Financial Stabilization Reserve, carried 13 to 0; (3) July 4, 2022, item 6.6 CO01277, $4.7 million from the Financial Stabilization Reserve for the 2022 portion of the 2022-2023 winter, carried 13 to 0. Amended budget 64,466 + 2,300 + 14,300 + 4,700 = 85,766; ratio 1.166; Contradicted under both cutoff sets. Without the March carry-forward, 83,466 and 1.198, still Contradicted under both. The other reviewers' July-only reading gives 69,166 and 1.446, Contradicted under primary cutoffs and Partially supported under alternative cutoffs. The City's own year-end 2022 Snow and Ice Control expense budget (Operating Financial Update - December 31, 2022, FCS01656 Attachment 1) is 79,474, giving 1.258, Contradicted under primary cutoffs and just Partially supported under alternative cutoffs; the year-end figure is lower than my summed amendments, so a reconciliation the City has not published (offsets or reallocations) sits between them. Alternative B, 2023 approved: the brief's named cell does not exist. The 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans (804 PDF pages, re-checked on 2026-09-02) has no Snow and Ice Control program summary table; the program appears on 14 pages as a service description, in the Enhanced Snow and Ice Control Service Standards package (page 105: 4,043 / 3,725 / 2,477 / 721 for 2023-2026 in $000s plus 275 in Community Standards and Neighbourhoods) and in the Parks and Roads Services branch section, which reports branch totals only. Operating Budget Amendment 18 (moved A. Sohi, carried 12 to 1, M. Janz opposed) funded that package at 20 per cent ongoing: 2023 $3,768,000 Parks and Roads plus $274,600 Community Standards. The nearest City figure for the 2023 program after the amendment is $60.9 million (City Budget Engagement Fact Sheet, undated as to year; Global News 2022-12-20 states it as the 2023 total; CBC 2022-12-16 reports a $56.9 million base plus the $4 million amendment, which sum to it). Ratio 100 / 60.9 = 1.642, Partially supported under both cutoff sets. Using the year-end 2023 adjusted expense budget of 63,574 (FCS02229 Attachment 1) instead: 1.573, Partially supported under both. Context, not denominators: 2022 'Total Net Operating Requirement' 63,653 ($000s; the branch summary on printed page 205 shows 63,666), ratio 1.571; 2022 actual gross expenditure 97,571 (FCS01656 Attachment 1; heavier snowfall and freezing rain, $13.0 million January to April and $5.0 million October to December over budget), ratio 1.025. Qualification 1, like-for-like: (a) 2023 approved CM-20-0330 5,950 against 2023 snow 60,900 = 0.098 (against 63,574: 0.094); the bike-lane allocation for 2023 was about one tenth of the year's snow budget. (b) $100 million against four years of approved snow budget: 60,900 (2023) + 67,090 (2024, year-end adjusted expense budget, FCS02841 Attachment 1) + 68,618 (2025 Approved Budget, FCS03370 Attachment 1 page 6) + 72,645 (2026 Approved Budget, same page) = 269,253; ratio 0.371. The four figures are not on one basis (see limitations). Qualification 2, actuals: CM-20-0330 by year by differencing cumulative to-date actuals: 2023 807 (FCS02228 Att. 2, Dec 31, 2023); 2024 10,496 - 807 = 9,689 (FCS02842 Att. 2); 2025 39,984 - 10,496 = 29,488 (FCS03313 Att. 2, Dec 31, 2025); total spent to December 31, 2025: 39,984, 40.2 per cent of the current 99,570 budget; actual average $13.3 million a year over three completed years against an approved average of $25.0 million. Snow and Ice Control actuals, program-summary basis (FCS03370): 51,750 / 64,749 / 66,588; ratios 0.016 (2023), 0.150 (2024), 0.443 (2025); three-year 39,984 / 183,087 = 0.218. On the Operating Financial Update basis (54,917 / 72,086 / 76,648): 0.015, 0.134, 0.385; three-year 0.196. Qualification 3: net figure ratio 1.571 as above. Qualification 4: no constant-dollar restatement applied; all figures nominal. Position after cross-review: unchanged. The other two reviewers reach the same primary ratio from the same cell; I keep Partially supported because 1.551 falls in the brief's band, not because they do. Where we differ is Alternative A, where I hold that the full amendment list makes the as-amended reading Contradicted under both cutoff sets. Definition sensitivity: primary Partially supported; Alternative A Contradicted; Alternative B Partially supported. The finding is definition-sensitive on the in-year amendment question and the story should say so beside the verdict.

PRIMARY: The 2022 Snow and Ice Control 'Expenditure & Transfers' cell is $64,466 (in $000s) on page 212 of the Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget. Ratio: 100,000 / 64,466 = 1.551. Verdict: Partially supported under both primary cutoffs (1.5 to <1.8) and alternative cutoffs (1.25 to <1.7). ALTERNATIVE A (amended 2022 budget): adding council amendments of $2.3M (March 14), $14.3M (April 19), and $4.7M (July 4) to the base $64.466M gives $85.766M. Ratio: 1.166. Verdict: Contradicted under both sets of cutoffs. ALTERNATIVE B (2023 budget): The 2023-2026 Operating Budget lacks a program summary for Snow and Ice Control. Using the City's 2023 adjusted expense budget of $63,574 (from Dec 2023 Operating Financial Update), the ratio is 1.573 (Partially supported). CONTEXT: 2022 Net Operating Requirement was $63,653. Actual 2022 snow expenditure was $97,571. QUALIFICATIONS: (1) Like-for-like 2023 ratio: CM-20-0330 2023 allocation ($5,950) vs 2023 adjusted snow budget ($63,574) = 0.094. (2) Whole program vs 4-year snow budgets: 100,000 / (63,574 [2023] + 67,090 [2024] + 67,554 [2025] + ~67,000 [2026 placeholder]) = 0.377. (3) Actuals: CM-20-0330 actuals were 807 (2023), 9,689 (2024), 29,488 (2025). Ratios to snow actuals: 0.015 (2023), 0.134 (2024), 0.385 (2025). (4) Approved average CM-20-0330 is $25M/year; actual average 2023-2025 is $13.3M/year.

PRIMARY: The capital profile was approved at $100.000 million, allocated $5.950 million in 2023, $26.750 million in 2024, $33.650 million in 2025 and $33.650 million in 2026. The operating-budget table is printed in thousands and gives 2022 Snow and Ice Control Expenditure & Transfers of $64.466 million. The ratio is 100/64.466 = 1.551, producing Partially supported under both the primary cutoffs and the alternative cutoffs. The failing element is 'almost double.' ALTERNATIVE A: The identified council additions are $2.3 million approved March 14, $14.3 million approved April 19 and $4.7 million approved July 4. Applying the brief's mechanical rule gives $64.466 million + $21.3 million = $85.766 million and a ratio of 1.166, Contradicted under both cutoff sets. The City's year-end table instead reports an adjusted expense budget of $79.474 million; 100/79.474 = 1.258, Contradicted under the primary cutoffs and Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs. The $6.292 million discrepancy is unresolved, so the additive figure should not be represented as a reconciled year-end budget. ALTERNATIVE B: The named 2023 Snow and Ice Control program-summary cell does not appear in the 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans. A City fact sheet reports $60.9 million, while the 2023 year-end financial update reports an adjusted expense budget of $63.574 million. Their ratios are 1.642 and 1.573 respectively, both Partially supported under both cutoff sets, but neither is the exact named adopted cell. CONTEXT: The printed 2022 Total Net Operating Requirement is $63.653 million, giving 1.571. The 2022 actual expense of $97.571 million gives 1.025, but actuals do not carry the verdict. LIKE FOR LIKE: The approved 2023 profile allocation was 5.950/60.9 = 0.098 using the fact-sheet snow figure, or 5.950/63.574 = 0.094 using the year-end adjusted budget. A defensible four-year approved-budget ratio cannot be completed without a sourced 2026 program budget. ACTUALS: CM-20-0330 cumulative actuals were $0.807 million at 2023 year-end, $10.496 million at 2024 year-end and $39.984 million at 2025 year-end, producing annual amounts of $0.807 million, $9.689 million and $29.488 million. Against the operating financial updates' snow actuals of $54.917 million, $72.086 million and $76.648 million, the annual ratios are 0.015, 0.134 and 0.385. A separate City program-reporting series gives lower snow actuals and must be reconciled before publication. Total profile spending through 2025 was $39.984 million; the original approved average was $25.000 million per year, and the 2023-2025 actual average was $13.328 million per year. A June 10, 2025 transfer reduced the current profile budget by $0.430 million to $99.570 million. No constant-dollar restatement was applied.

reviewers.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY BOUNDARY, verified against every profile sheet (I parsed the 'Service Category:' field on all 161 profile sheets in the adopted document): 20 sheets carry 'Roads' and 11 carry 'Neighbourhood Renewal'; the membership matches the editor's reading exactly, and the three bridge profiles carry no Service Category as the brief says. Amounts (2023-2026 total, $000s, Appendix A page): ROADS: 18-66-6503 50 Street CPR Grade Separation 94,202 (p.103); 19-22-9006 Terwillegar Drive Expressway Upgrades - Alternate Staging 119,200 + 41,821 = 161,021 (both lines, p.104); 21-20-9301 Yellowhead Trail 156 Street to St Albert Trail 54,634 (p.104); 21-20-9302 Yellowhead Trail Fort Road Widening 54,597 (p.104); 21-40-9031 Winterburn Industrial Road Upgrading 12 (p.104); 21-40-9032 Mistatim/Southeast Industrial Road Upgrading 10 (p.103); 22-22-9700 124 Street 109 to 118 Avenue 10,056 (p.102); 22-22-9701 Gateway Blvd Renewal 5,094 (p.103); CM-20-2020 Transportation Planning and Design - Growth 9,007 (p.104); CM-22-0000 Goods Movement - Arterial Renewal 64,843 (p.104); CM-24-0000 Bridges & Auxiliary Structures - Renewal 209,836 (p.104); CM-26-0000 Traffic Systems - Renewal 9,308 (p.104); CM-66-2194 Regulated Safety Upgrades at Railway Crossings 720 (p.104); CM-66-2525 Traffic Signals - Developer and ARA Funded 16,000 (p.104); CM-66-2585 Safe Crossings 25,875 (p.101); CM-66-2596 Safe and Livable Community Streets 17,148 (p.101); CM-99-0060 Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion: Project Development 7,914 (p.104); CM-99-9600 Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion: Project Delivery 376,255 (p.104); subtotal Roads 1,116,532. NEIGHBOURHOOD RENEWAL (all p.101): 20-40-9017 4,658; 20-40-9019 721; 21-40-9023 14,652; 21-40-9024 22,047; 21-40-9025 9,780; 21-40-9026 2,100; 21-40-9027 464; 22-40-9028 17,130; 22-40-9029 23,710; CM-25-0000 Transportation: Neighbourhoods - Renewal 545,717; CM-27-0000 Neighbourhood Alley Renewal 81,310; subtotal 722,289. BRIDGES (p.103): 23-24-0300 High Level Bridge Rehabilitation 97,000; 21-24-9301 Latta Bridge Replacement 9,832; 21-24-9302 Glenora Bridge Renewal 50; subtotal 106,882. PRIMARY TOTAL 1,945,703 ($1,945.7 million), ratio to $100 million = 19.46 -> Supported under the primary cutoffs (>= $1.5 billion) and under the alternative cutoffs (>= $1.62 billion). REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE: Table 8 'Adopted Capital Budget by Service', page 56, 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' 2023-2026: Growth 622.8, Renewal 1,171.2, Total $1,794.0 million (2027 and beyond 108.6; overall 1,902.6); ratio 17.94 -> Supported under both cutoff sets. This line is the combined service allocation including CM-20-0330 and other active-pathway funding; it is not a roads total. NARROWEST (Service Category 'Roads' only): $1,116.5 million, 11.17x -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets (the failing part is the figure). WIDEST (primary plus 21-50-9101 103 Avenue Streetscape 560, 21-50-9100 103A Avenue Pedway 25,400, 17-74-4103 Jasper Avenue New Vision Phase 2 265, CM-20-3102 Chinatown Infrastructure Improvements 10,100, CM-20-3100 Missing and Enhanced Sidewalk Connections 13,615, 20-20-2024 Edmonton-Strathcona County Pedestrian Bridge 30,205; extras 80,145): $2,025.8 million, 20.26x -> Supported. Sheets whose label differs from the editor's reading: none. Two profiles with blank Service Category that a reader might expect under roads were not included under any reading, per the brief: CM-29-0000 Transportation - Minor Renewal Program (15,000, p.104) and 21-31-9100 Rundle Park Road and Parking Lot Renewal (181, p.104). ADDITIONAL SENSITIVITY, reported not carrying the verdict: the four Yellowhead Trail profiles (CM-99-9600, CM-99-0060, 21-20-9301, 21-20-9302; 493,400 combined) carry Service Category 'Roads' on their sheets but Table 8 reports them as the transformational project 'Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion' ($493.4 million), outside 'Active Pathways and Roads Service'. Removing them from the primary gives $1,452.3 million, 14.5x -> Partially supported under both cutoff sets; removing them from the narrowest gives $623.1 million, 6.2x -> Contradicted. THE '180': Global News (2022-12-12, Stephanie Swensrude) quotes Councillor Janz: 'Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.' $1.8 billion is 18 times $100 million, not 180; the figure appears only in that article; the council minutes do not record debate speech, and no other coverage I found repeats the sentence with either number. The councillor's own campaign page states 'The $100M represents half a percent of the $1.8 Billion dollar capital budget over the same period', which is also arithmetically wrong (it is 5.6 per cent); it confirms the $1.8 billion figure is the councillor's, and that figure matches Table 8's 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' total of $1,794.0 million. QUALIFICATION 2 (as amended): a roads-only as-amended total cannot be computed from published documents because composite renewal profiles (CM-25-0000, CM-24-0000, CM-22-0000) are split into standalone project profiles as work is approved and the City publishes no roads total; the whole-budget trajectory is: tax-supported 2023-2026 capital budget $9,073 million after 2022 carry-forwards (Fall 2024 SCBA Attachment 1); Spring 2024 SCBA approved 2024-06-11 (CBC: capital budget increased to $10.4 billion); Fall 2024 SCBA approved 2024-12-02, net +$151.8 million tax-supported; Fall 2025 SCBA 2025-11-24, net +$98.2 million, total capital budget after Fall 2025 SCBA $11,612 million (all years); final adjustment 2026-06-16, +$126.6 million (1.10%) on an $11.56 billion capital budget (City webpage). Yellowhead Trail total approved budget: $630.6 million (Dec 31, 2023), $756.1 million (Dec 31, 2024), $750.2 million (Dec 31, 2025); Terwillegar Drive 19-22-9006 total profile budget $284.7 million (Dec 2023) and $327.2 million (Dec 2024 onward, after a $41.0 million provincial grant recosting in the Fall 2024 SCBA); High Level Bridge 23-24-0300 total profile $200.0 million throughout. CM-20-0330 amendment: Spring 2025 SCBA (FCS02852 Attachment 4, council 2025-06-10) transferred $430,000 of tax-supported debt from CM-20-0330 to new profile 25-25-9506 Dunluce Neighbourhood and Alley Renewal; the profile's current approved budget is $99,570 thousand from the September 30, 2025 update onward. QUALIFICATION 3 (actuals): the City does not publish roads capital expenditure by year; profile to-date actuals as of December 31, 2025 ($000s): Terwillegar 19-22-9006 209,132 (of 327,220); Yellowhead Trail 2023-2026 expenditures $132.7 million (Capital Results attachment); High Level Bridge 4,635; CM-24-0000 26,360; CM-22-0000 16,841; CM-66-2585 17,897; CM-25-0000 28,029 (composite remainder only). CM-20-0330 to-date actuals: 807 (Dec 31, 2023), 10,496 (Dec 31, 2024), 25,093 (Sept 30, 2025), 39,984 (Dec 31, 2025); by year 807 / 9,689 / 29,488; total spent to Dec 31, 2025 $39,984 thousand of $99,570 thousand (40 per cent); approved average $25,000 thousand a year, actual average 2023-2025 $13,328 thousand a year. QUALIFICATION 4 (shares, approved figures): CM-20-0330 $100.0 million = 1.26% of the $7.91 billion adopted 2023-2026 capital budget (Table 8 total); 1.39% of the $7,192.5 million Appendix A tax-supported profile total; 4.43% of 'Total Movement of People and Goods' $2,256.0 million; 5.57% of 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' $1,794.0 million; 1.95% of transportation defined as Movement of People and Goods plus LRT Expansion ($2,374.9 million) plus Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion ($493.4 million) = $5,124.3 million. PROGRAM STATUS CONTEXT: report IS03688 (Infrastructure Committee 2026-08-26) says about 35 km of routes were installed in 2024-2025 with 24 km estimated for 2026, and recommended a modified approach; the committee's minutes show a motion to continue the program per the approved scope of CM-20-0330 was defeated 2-2 and the recommendation was not adopted; the committee heard from more than 60 registered speakers.

The sum of the primary boundary roads-only profiles is $1.946 billion, which exceeds the $1.5 billion threshold for a 'Supported' verdict. The required alternative Table 8 lists the 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' at $1,794.0 million. The narrowest reading (Service Category 'Roads' only, without Neighbourhood Renewal or bridges) totals $1.117 billion. The speaker's statement contained a mathematical error ('180 times as much' rather than 18 times).

Summing the prescribed adopted profile amounts produces $1.945703 billion: $1.116532 billion in profiles labelled Roads, $722.289 million in profiles labelled Neighbourhood Renewal and $106.882 million for the three included vehicle-carrying bridge profiles without a service-category label. The ratio to $100 million is 19.457. This is Supported under both the primary and alternative cutoffs. The required alternative is Table 8's combined "Active Pathways and Roads Service" allocation of $1.7940 billion, or 17.94 times; it is also Supported under both cutoff sets but is not a roads-only total and includes active-pathway funding. The primary exceeds the combined service line because the brief's profile-label boundary also captures profiles presented under separate service or transformational lines, including Traffic Safety and Yellowhead Trail work. The narrowest Roads-labelled-only reading is $1.116532 billion, or 11.165 times, which is Partially supported under both cutoff sets.
